subject: religious-studies
title: Augustine on Human Nature
welcome_lead: Sit with the Bishop of Hippo as he meditates on the disordered will, the goodness of creation, and the necessity of grace.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on Augustine's anthropology: the Fall, original sin, concupiscence, and the necessity of grace.
final_note: You have grasped Augustine's account of human nature: created good, fallen in Adam, healed only by Christ's grace.

walkthroughs.h2: The Garden and the Pear Tree
walkthroughs.body_html: In Confessions II.4, Augustine narrates stealing pears as a boy 'not because I was hungry. but simply because it was not allowed'. The story illustrates his account of sin as perverse love: turning from God to a creature for its own sake. His Confessions, written around 397-400 AD, is a sustained meditation on grace ('thou hast made us for thyself, and our heart is restless until it rests in thee').

Augustine reads Genesis 3 (with Romans 5:12) as the historical occasion of a corruption transmitted to all humanity. After the Fall, the will retains freedom of choice but is in bondage to sin (non posse non peccare). Concupiscence, especially as disordered sexuality, transmits original sin biologically. Only baptism removes its guilt; concupiscence as wound remains.

Pelagius rejected Augustine's pessimism; the Synod of Carthage (418) sided with Augustine. The Council of Orange (529) confirmed prevenient grace. Modern critics like Reinhold Niebuhr accept the diagnosis but reinterpret it existentially. Feminist theologians criticise Augustine's reading of Eve and his treatment of sexuality as the vehicle of sin.

mcqs.q: Augustine's Latin phrase for fallen humanity's inability not to sin is:
options: posse non peccare
non posse non peccare
non posse peccare
posse peccare

mcqs.q: The famous opening prayer of the Confessions ends 'our heart is ___ until it rests in thee'.
options: weary
empty
restless
broken

mcqs.q: What was the Augustine vs Pelagius dispute about original sin?
options: Original sin means Christians believe babies are evil.
Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.

Augustine argued humans inherit a corrupted nature from Adam (original sin) and cannot achieve salvation without grace; Pelagius argued humans retain free will to choose good without divine intervention and that sin is imitated, not inherited.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.

mcqs.q: What does Kant's categorical imperative require?
options: Acting only on maxims you could will to be universal laws, and treating people as ends in themselves, never merely as means.
Treat others how you would like to be treated.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
